Training pathway, 2017-2026 20 provinces, 739 pairs +3.27 with all coded records, +3.27 for common routes, +3.27 with common routes weighted equally Cutoffs reached earlier ranks in these endpoint-matched schools over the full decade.

318

In the examination-category analysis, growth in the reference population offset 319 part of the rank-based decline (Table 1). The supplement gives field availability and 320 source-level plan reconciliation for all 310 province-years and the 100-cell source 321 audit. 322

Endpoint source verification 323

For the 2026 endpoint, published provincial distributions reproduced the frozen 324 candidate denominator for 1,085 of 1,771 programme records (61.3%) across nine 325 examination systems. The reproduced records included 904 exact-score tie endpoints 326 confirmed independently. They also included 171 Shandong records that reported 327 rank without a score, two records assigned the top-threshold endpoint and eight 328 records assigned an endpoint above the top threshold. The remaining 686 records 329 retained frozen source metadata without an independent denominator check. The 330 endpoint audit therefore counted programme records, whereas the national trajectory 331 sample counted 1,708 province-school pairs after school-level aggregation. For the 332 post hoc 2023-2026 comparison, requiring all 2026 records in a province-school unit 333 to be independently verified retained 772 matched pairs in nine systems. All nine 334 provincial medians moved later, with a province-equal mean change of -5.64 points (Table S12). At the 2023 endpoint, 2,150 of 2,165 records matched a unique exact score in a multi-year public compilation. This count included 15 Xinjiang records reproduced from a reprint. These checks assess existing reference denominators and add no observations to the national endpoint estimate.

One paired programme record illustrates the endpoint calculation. Xi'an Medical University published 524 places for its ordinary five-year clinical medicine programme in Shaanxi before preferences opened in 2023 and 517 in 2024. Both cohorts were filled. The minimum score rose from 508 to 526, while the tied cutoff moved from ranks 27,965-28,337 of 166,437 to 31,870-32,295 of 174,874 (top 16.80%-17.03% and 18.22%-18.47%). Programme applications were unavailable. This single programme checks the capacity-percentile relation and does not change the national estimate. 24, 25

National admission-plan source audit

A total of 100 province-year cells across 30 provincial systems lacked a verified initial provincial plan total. These cells were audited. The registry contained 441 candidate plan rows and 492 links to admission records. Thirty-seven candidate values matched the frozen admission count, four field conflicts were adjudicated and two pre-choice plan values had independent dates. One cell contained both a verified plan and admission value. No complete provincial plan total was constructed (Table S13).

An additional project-level audit covered 110 province-university-programmeyear units at three institutions across 26 origin systems in 2023-2026. Every unit had a published plan and a minimum admission boundary. Actual admissions were explicit for 78 units and first-parallel-round admissions for 16. The remaining 16 had a published plan and minimum boundary but no usable admitted count. None provided a matched count of all first-programme choices at the same province-schoolprogramme grain (Table S14). A separate school-wide count at Chengdu University in 2023 recorded 265 first-programme choices and 91 admissions without a provincespecific denominator. It was not added to the panel. These records broaden the source audit for plans and boundaries. They do not establish a national capacity total or a national applicant-demand series.

Discussion

A late-decade reversal

At the 2017 and 2026 endpoints, the matched-school estimate for 754 provinceschool pairs was +3.02 percentile points, whereas the annual-sample estimate was -3.90. The direction of the full-period change therefore depended on school and province coverage. In the continuously observed 15-province panel, the observed maximum occurred in 2023, with a province-equal mean of 86.06, followed by 76.51 in 2026. In the post hoc 2023-2026 comparison, provincial medians moved later in 25 of 29 comparable provinces, with a mean change of -5.65 percentile points. This recent direction remained stable across school-identity definitions and within the 15province matched examination-population subset.

In the 2023-2025 comparison, provincial medians moved later in 25 of 29 provinces, with a mean change of -2.31 points. This shows that the recent direction was already present before the dominant 2026 source transition, although other source, coverage and measurement influences cannot be excluded. The 2023-2026 magnitude was larger and remained coverage-sensitive. The 2026 fixed-panel mean was close to its 2017 level, concentrating the reversal in the later years of the series.

The annual-availability estimate remained 3.90 points below its 2017 level. The near-stable 407-pair continuous panel and the +3.02 endpoint estimate for 754 pairs reflect different sample compositions, including 15 versus 20 provinces and different continuing-school requirements.

Career conditions and the relative appeal of medicine

Applicants assess medicine before they experience medical work. Their expectations may draw on training length, physicians' reported conditions and the credential requirements they anticipate when seeking a clinical post. Available records are dated, discontinuous and differently sampled. Together they identify conditions present during the decade in which reported cutoffs moved, without forming a continuous national series.

Long working weeks appeared in each separately sampled survey. A 2015 national tertiary-hospital survey recorded a mean of 50.5 patient-service hours per week. 15 A 2017-2018 national tertiary-hospital survey found that about one in five physicians considered leaving the profession. 16 A 2018 survey of 2,915 physicians in 48 public hospitals across six provinces found that 88.9% worked more than 40 hours per week and 35.3% worked more than 60 hours. 26 In a 2019 survey of 22,213 physicians at 144 tertiary public hospitals in all 31 provincial systems, mean working time was 9.62 hours per day and 66.54% worked more than eight hours per day. 18 A national online survey conducted in 2020 and reported in 2021 included 12,930 physicians across 28 provincial systems. It recorded 7.77 clinical hours per day, 1.47 research hours per day and 5.77 working days per week. 19 A 2024 survey of 1,324 physicians in four provincial-level regions reported a mean of 49.4 total weekly hours. 20 Repeated psychiatric-hospital surveys recorded 47.1, 53.0 and 50.3 hours per week in 2017, 2019 and 2021. 27, 28, 29 The estimands differed, but every sample reported a long-hours profile.

National hospital statistics show the same service intensity across the wider delivery system. In 2023, general hospitals recorded 7.2 outpatient visits and 2.2 inpatient bed-days per physician per working day, compared with 6.8 visits and 1.9 bed-days in 2022. The 2024 yearbook also supplied province-level hospital workload values for all 31 provincial systems. 30 These measures capture direct service volume and exclude teaching, research, administration and waiting time.

The only repeated relative-earnings series covered 2016-2019. Its source-defined earnings ratio, calculated from after-tax physician income and gross average urban employee earnings, was 1.54, 1.92, 1.50 and 1.48; the recorded ratio declined after 2017. 17 The two components use different tax bases. Three further records provide dated standalone benchmarks. Mean annual pay was RMB 108,334 in a 2017 payroll study of 178,622 licensed physicians across 21 provinces. 21 More than half of respondents reported monthly income below RMB 7,500 in the 2020 online survey. 19 Mean self-reported monthly income was RMB 8,245.1 in the 2024 four-region survey. 20 These records use different samples, periods and remuneration definitions and were not treated as a continuous income series.

The length and structure of training add another entry cost. Clinical medicine includes five-year, integrated five-plus-three, six-year and eight-year routes. In the 2021 and 2022 national entrant cohorts, 84.76% and 78.39% of respondents expected further study before employment. 14, 13 Credential requirements varied across two distinct recruitment frames (Table S15, Supplementary Figure S2). 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 Position lines and advertised places were different units from separate recruitment frames, and no hospital-tier effect was estimated.

These records describe long and heterogeneous training pathways, high service loads, varied recruitment requirements and a source-defined relative-earnings ratio that declined after 2017. Together, these conditions support a hypothesis of lower perceived net returns from medicine. The late-decade admission shift could reflect how entrants and families weighed these conditions alongside security, status and service mission, but applicant perceptions were not measured. Admission plans, applicant pools, programme composition, eligibility rules and allocation rules could also have contributed.

A 2026 discrete-choice experiment surveyed 555 clinical master's and doctoral graduates. Pre-tax monthly income (33.7% relative importance) and job location (24.0%) were the most important attributes, and workload, career development, permanent-establishment status and working environment also influenced choices. 31 A national registration cohort recorded at least one change of practice institution for 725,424 of 3,748,224 full-time licensed physicians between 2011 and 2021; registry exits included retirement and did not identify voluntary career change. 22 These findings map the career stage after admission and show which working conditions graduates value. They do not connect those preferences to the applicants whose reported cutoffs moved.

Career intentions and public accounts

A 2020, 24-province survey conducted during the COVID-19 period recorded how 21,085 senior-high students described medicine. Among 11,121 respondents who did not intend to apply, lack of interest was selected most often, followed by violence risk (18.5%), workload (17.5%), long training (17.3%) and high responsibility (14.7%). Low income was selected by 3.6%. 23 In this non-applicant subgroup, 47.3% came from Sichuan. The most visible objections concerned the nature of the work and its risks, with long training and workload more prominent than low income. These intentions were measured before application and allocation. The available application-stage evidence is limited to a 2017-2019 Beijing statistical series and individual programme archives; it shows that application pressure and admission boundaries can move together or diverge as places and allocation rules change. 32 The cutoff records a published filing-or-admission boundary, while surveys and application records describe earlier expectations and choices.

Provincial divergence

The national direction contains substantial provincial variation. From 2023 to 2026, cutoffs moved later in nine of ten eastern, five of five central, eight of eleven western and three of three northeastern systems. The equal-province mean changes were -8.31, -6.59, -2.70 and -6.07 percentile points. The direction therefore appeared across all four broad regions, with different magnitudes.

Local school supply, the mix of examination categories, candidate migration, living costs and the composition of hospital posts can produce different regional combinations of opportunity and pressure. Provinces with a larger supply of medical places may record a later cutoff without an equivalent change in the number of applicants. Provinces with limited places can retain an earlier cutoff even as interest weakens. Migration between provincial systems adds a further source of variation.

The present data cannot assign a regional mechanism or estimate how much each condition contributed.

International admission systems and labour-market signals

Comparisons with other admission systems clarify what a cutoff can and cannot represent. Portugal and Denmark publish first-choice numbers alongside medicalprogramme admission boundaries, but the two stages do not move in lockstep. 33, 34 Quotas, programme capacity and allocation rules intervene between expressed preference and the final boundary. A first-choice count records demand at an earlier stage; a cutoff records the published boundary at the filing or admission stage, rather than applicant demand itself. Japan provides a long-run counterpoint. Medical-school selectivity increased from 1980 to 2017 during prolonged economic stagnation, and occupational stability was one proposed interpretation. 35 This account suggests a contextual hypothesis: when secure employment and predictable earnings carry a high premium, medicine can become more selective even under adverse economic conditions. A later weakening of that premium could accompany the opposite movement as alternative careers improve or confidence in the relative security of medicine declines. The Japanese case does not imply that the two countries share a common trajectory or that the proposed conditions caused the Chinese reversal.

Costs recorded in the United Kingdom and the United States provide parallel labour-market context rather than additional evidence on Chinese trends. In the United Kingdom, 42% of responding doctors in training reported heavy or very heavy workloads. In the United States, 70% of the 2025 graduating survey reported education debt, with a median of USD 215,000 among indebted respondents. 36, 37 Chinese entrants face a long domestic training route and a recruitment market differentiated by institution. American entrants face a large financial entry cost. British trainees face sustained service pressure. In each setting, medicine competes with other careers on security, earnings, working conditions and the time required to establish a career.

International comparisons show that applicant preferences and final admission cutoffs are distinct quantities. They provide contextual hypotheses but do not identify the mechanisms underlying the changes observed in China. Admission institutions determine where any such change becomes visible: in first-choice counts, application ratios, interview selection or the final cutoff. The Chinese series uses published filingor-admission boundaries across a large and institutionally diverse national system.

Interpretation and research implications

The central contribution is a province-equal national account of how reported clinical medicine cutoffs changed over a decade and how that account depends on school and province coverage. The recent reversal survives within-school, schoolidentity and examination-category comparisons, while its magnitude remains coverage-sensitive. The full-period direction changes when coverage definitions change. Separately sampled records document long hours, long and heterogeneous training, a source-defined relative-earnings ratio that declined after 2017, varied recruitment requirements across two frames in 2025-2026, and hesitation among prospective students. These records provide context around the admission series but do not estimate the causes of the cutoff changes. The contextual evidence consists of single-year snapshots and short repeated cross-sections. Recruitment evidence comes from readable public schedules in leading hospitals or one national hospital group; advertised requirements describe vacancies and leave completed hiring unobserved. The physician surveys concentrate on tertiary public hospitals, and the psychiatric series is specialty-specific with changing hospital coverage. The 2020 survey covered 24 provincial systems, and non-applicant responses were concentrated in Sichuan. The 2017 payroll study and the repeated earnings surveys use different samples and remuneration definitions. International sources use different admission stages, institutions and sampling frames. These materials support interpretation of the national admission series and provide a comparative framework for future measurement. The domestic evidence-coverage table records the available denominator and principal limit for each contextual source family (Table S16).

Conclusions

Clinical medicine admission cutoffs in China reached an observed maximum in the 15-province fixed panel in 2023 and subsequently moved later in most comparable provinces. This post hoc recent direction appeared under alternative school identities and within the matched examination-population subset, although its magnitude remained coverage-sensitive. The 2023-2025 comparison showed that the direction predated the main 2026 source transition. Across the full decade, the direction depended on school and province coverage. Long hours, a source-defined relativeearnings ratio that declined after 2017, long and heterogeneous training pathways, varied recruitment requirements across two distinct frames, and hesitation among prospective students describe the career context but do not identify the causes of the cutoff changes. International comparisons distinguish applicant preferences from final admission cutoffs and provide contextual hypotheses rather than causal evidence. Linking applicants, available places and career outcomes within the same cohorts is the next step for testing whether and how these conditions enter that choice.

Ethics approval and consent to participate

This study used publicly available aggregate records and did not involve human participants or individually identifiable data. Institutional ethics review was not required.

Figure 1.

Figure 1. Annual clinical medicine cutoffs and source coverage. Panel a shows the equal-province mean of provincial medians for annually available schools and the 407 province-school pairs observed in all ten years. Higher percentiles indicate earlier examination ranks. Panel b shows annual counts of contributing provinces (bars, left scale) and province-school pairs (line, right scale).

Figure 2.

Figure 2. Provincial clinical medicine cutoff levels and cumulative changes. Provinces follow the standard administrative-region order: North, Northeast, East, Central, South, Southwest and Northwest. Horizontal rules mark the regional boundaries. Panel a shows the annual median cutoff percentile on a 0-100 scale. Panel b shows cumulative change in percentile points from the first year in which that province met the three-school threshold. Hatched cells indicate fewer than three schools; grey cells indicate no usable value. Higher percentiles indicate earlier examination positions, and negative changes indicate movement towards later positions.

Figure 3.

Figure 3. Sequential coverage-frame adjustments to estimated changes in candidate-referenced clinical medicine admission-cutoff percentiles. In each panel, the first and fourth bars show the province-equal estimates for schools matched at both endpoints and for the annually available sample. The middle bars show sequential changes from including unpaired schools within matched provinces and then expanding province coverage. These steps are sample adjustments that depend on their order. They should not be read as independent effects, causal contributions or corrections for nonrandom missingness. School-unit counts show the numbers of schools observed at the starting and ending endpoints; matched pairs are counted once at baseline. The 0.00 province-coverage adjustment in 2025-2026 indicates that no additional provinces entered at the final step and was zero by construction. Negative values indicate movement towards later candidate ranks. Components are rounded separately. Uncertainty intervals are not shown.

Provincial applicant counts, first choices and complete place totals would separate demand from capacity and score distribution. Repeated provincial measures of physician hours, earnings and recruitment would show whether conditions recorded in separate snapshots moved with the national admission series. Following applicants through medical school, postgraduate training and the first clinical post could test whether a later cutoff predicts later entry, exit or migration within the profession. A linked applicant-cohort design is the next step for testing whether and how these conditions enter that choice. Limitations Thirty-one provincial systems entered the frame, 30 contributed to at least one annual estimate and 28-30 contributed in each year from 2021 to 2026. Tibet had no province-year cell with three schools, and Henan lacked a qualifying common-school comparison for 2023-2026. Programme composition, examination categories and source families changed within and between provinces, particularly in 2026. Subjecteligibility rules and admission-batch structures also changed across provinces during the study period and could alter the eligible applicant pool within a reported examination distribution. The annual sample contained 1,708 province-school pairs in 2026, compared with 2,534 in 2025. Fixed-school and category-level analyses preserved the direction of the recent result without treating the annual-sample difference as a demand estimate. Sources sometimes referred to filing and sometimes to completed admission, and stage was not recorded consistently. Part of the change may therefore reflect stage composition. Independent source checks reproduced the reference denominator for 1,085 of 1,771 2026 programme records (61.3%) and matched 2,150 of 2,165 2023 records at a unique exact score. The reproduced count comprised 904 exact-score tie endpoints, 171 reported ranks from Shandong, two top-threshold endpoints and eight values above the published top threshold. The remaining records retained frozen source metadata and were not treated as directly reproduced.
